ready1_open_rewrite.title: SciVerse open question
ready1_open_rewrite.rewritten_question_text: A certain binary mixture contains solute A at 25\%, and single-stage extraction is proposed. At the operating temperature, the obtained solubility curve is as shown in the figure. After adding solvent S, the content of A in the obtained extract is $Y_{EA} = 40\%$; within this operating range, the distribution coefficient of solute A is $K_{A} = 1.0$. Find the content of A in the raffinate of this extraction process, $X_{RA}$.

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: the figure is a triangular solubility diagram, with vertex A at the upper left, vertex B at the lower left, and pure solvent S at the lower right; the left side is vertically marked with an A content scale from 0 to 1.0. In the figure there is a two-liquid-phase solubility curve, and the right branch intersects several operating lines. Near the A content 0.40 on the left side, E_A^* is marked; the straight line from that point down to the right to the pure solvent endpoint S intersects the right branch of the solubility curve at point E. From the figure, the actual A content vertical coordinate of point E is read as about 0.16. Reasoning: the problem gives the content of A in the extract as Y_EA=40%; according to the graphical method, first find E_A^*=0.40 on the left side, and connect E_A^* with S, intersecting the right branch of the solubility curve at the actual extract phase point E, so the actual mass fraction of A in the extract is Y_A≈0.16. Also, the problem gives the distribution coefficient in this range as K_A=Y_A/X_RA=1.0, so X_RA=Y_A/K_A≈0.16/1.0=0.16.
